# aria-skills-marketplace

An interactive skills marketplace plugin for [opencode](https://opencode.ai) 2.x. Browse, install, and auto-update skills directly from a GitLab registry — all from inside the opencode TUI.

## Features

- **`/aria-skills-marketplace` command** — searchable dialog to browse, install, update, and remove skills
- **No restart required** — an installed or updated skill is available in the session you installed it from
- **Auto-update on startup** — fetches the registry and installs updates for every installed skill, then reports what changed
- **GitLab-backed registry** — skills live in a GitLab repo you control
- **Multi-file skills** — each skill is a folder (`SKILL.md` + scripts, assets, references)
- **Versioned skills** — semver versioning, automatic updates on opencode start
- **Six tools for the model** — the agent can search and install skills on its own

## Requirements

opencode **2.0.32 or newer**. This is the 2.x line of the plugin and uses the V2 plugin API.

> Running opencode 1.x? Install `@aria-plugins/aria-skills-marketplace@^1` instead — V1 and V2
> plugin modules are not interchangeable, and a 1.x plugin will be rejected by opencode 2 with
> *"Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function."*

---

## Installation

### 1. Register the plugin

Add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`, with your registry details as options:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@aria-plugins/aria-skills-marketplace",
      "options": {
        "url": "https://gitlab.com/your-group/your-skills-registry",
        "token": "glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

opencode installs the package itself — there is no separate `npm install` step, and no
`~/.config/opencode/plugins/*.js` re-export shim (that was a V1 requirement; delete it if you
still have one).

If you would rather keep the token out of a config file, drop the `options` block and export the
environment variables instead:

```bash
export OPENCODE_MARKETPLACE_GITLAB_URL="https://gitlab.com/your-group/your-skills-registry"
export OPENCODE_MARKETPLACE_GITLAB_TOKEN="glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

Options win over the environment when both are set. The GitLab token needs `read_api` scope.

### 2. Register the TUI half

The marketplace dialog ships as a separate CLI plugin. Add the package to
`~/.config/opencode/cli.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@aria-plugins/aria-skills-marketplace"]
}
```

Unlike `opencode.jsonc`, `cli.json` is global only — opencode 2 reads one terminal-client config,
not a layered set.

### 3. Restart opencode

On the next start the plugin auto-updates installed skills, registers the six `marketplace_*`
tools, and claims the `/aria-skills-marketplace` command. Confirm it loaded with:

```bash
opencode plugin list
```

You should see `aria.skills-marketplace` with a version. An empty ID column means the module was
rejected — check `opencode api plugin.list` for the error.

---

## Usage

Type `/aria-skills-marketplace` in the opencode TUI, or pick **Skills Marketplace** from the
command palette, to open the marketplace:

```
Skills Marketplace  (12 available, 3 installed)
Search skills…

INSTALLED
  example-skill            v4.0.0 — installed                      ✓ up to date
  web-design-guidelines    v1.0.0 — update available → v1.1.0       ↑ update available

AVAILABLE
  Git Commit Helper        Writes conventional commits             v1.0.0  ·  git, commits
  Code Reviewer            Reviews pull requests                   v2.0.1  ·  code-review

SETTINGS
  Configure GitLab Connection
```

Pick an available skill to install it, or an installed one to update or remove it. Installs and
removals take effect immediately — opencode re-scans skills in place, so there is nothing to
restart.

Outside the TUI — `opencode run`, or any client without the CLI plugin — the same slash command
runs an agent-driven version of the flow using the tools below.

### Available AI tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `marketplace_status` | Sync status + list of installed skills |
| `marketplace_list` | Browse all registry skills (optional tag filter) |
| `marketplace_search` | Search skills by keyword across name, description, and tags |
| `marketplace_install` | Install a skill by ID |
| `marketplace_uninstall` | Remove an installed skill |
| `marketplace_update` | Update one skill or all skills with newer versions |

---

## Configuration

Set these as plugin `options` in `opencode.jsonc`, or as environment variables. Options take
precedence.

| Option | Environment variable | Required | Description |
|--------|----------------------|----------|-------------|
| `url` | `OPENCODE_MARKETPLACE_GITLAB_URL` | Yes | Full HTTPS URL to the GitLab skills registry repo |
| `token` | `OPENCODE_MARKETPLACE_GITLAB_TOKEN` | Yes | GitLab personal access token (`read_api` scope) |

`gitlabUrl` / `gitlabToken` are accepted as option aliases.

Skills install into `~/.config/opencode/skills/<skill-id>/`, which opencode 2 discovers
automatically — no `skills` path entry needed.

---

## GitLab Registry Structure

Your GitLab repository must follow this layout:

```
your-skills-registry/          ← the repo pointed to by OPENCODE_MARKETPLACE_GITLAB_URL
├── registry.json              ← root index listing all skills
└── skills/
    └── your-skill-id/
        ├── skill.json         ← skill manifest (id, version, tags, file list)
        ├── SKILL.md           ← AI instructions — required, must have frontmatter
        ├── references/        ← optional reference docs the AI reads
        ├── scripts/           ← optional helper scripts
        └── assets/            ← optional binary assets
```

### `registry.json` — root index

Lists every skill available in the registry. Update this file whenever you add or version a skill.

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "updated": "2026-05-21T00:00:00Z",
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "git-commit-helper",
      "name": "Git Commit Helper",
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "description": "Writes conventional commits and crafts perfect commit messages",
      "author": "your-username",
      "tags": ["git", "commits", "conventional-commits"],
      "path": "skills/git-commit-helper",
      "updatedAt": "2026-05-21T00:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "code-reviewer",
      "name": "Code Reviewer",
      "version": "2.0.1",
      "description": "Reviews pull requests and suggests improvements",
      "author": "your-username",
      "tags": ["code-review", "quality"],
      "path": "skills/code-reviewer",
      "updatedAt": "2026-04-10T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Unique slug — used as the folder name and install identifier |
| `name` | string | Display name shown in the marketplace UI |
| `version` | string | Semver version (e.g. `1.2.0`) — must match `skill.json` |
| `description` | string | One-line description shown in skill listings |
| `author` | string | Author name or username |
| `tags` | string[] | Searchable tags |
| `path` | string | Path to the skill folder relative to the repo root |
| `updatedAt` | string | ISO-8601 timestamp of the last update |

### `skill.json` — skill manifest

Lives inside each skill folder. Declares metadata and the full list of files the installer should download.

```json
{
  "id": "git-commit-helper",
  "name": "Git Commit Helper",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Writes conventional commits and crafts perfect commit messages",
  "author": "your-username",
  "tags": ["git", "commits", "conventional-commits"],
  "license": "MIT",
  "files": {
    "skillMd": "SKILL.md",
    "references": [
      "references/conventional-commits.md",
      "references/examples.md"
    ],
    "scripts": [
      "scripts/validate-message.sh"
    ],
    "assets": []
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Must match the folder name and `registry.json` entry |
| `name` | string | Display name |
| `version` | string | Semver version — bump this to trigger auto-updates |
| `description` | string | Short description |
| `author` | string | Author |
| `tags` | string[] | Searchable tags |
| `license` | string | Optional — SPDX license identifier |
| `files.skillMd` | string | Relative path to the `SKILL.md` file (always `"SKILL.md"`) |
| `files.references` | string[] | Reference docs loaded alongside the skill |
| `files.scripts` | string[] | Helper scripts bundled with the skill |
| `files.assets` | string[] | Binary or static assets (images, data files, etc.) |

### `SKILL.md` — AI instructions

Every skill **must** include a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Without the frontmatter, opencode will not recognise the file as a skill and it will not appear in `/skills`.

```markdown
---
name: git-commit-helper
description: Write conventional commits and craft perfect commit messages. Trigger when the user asks to commit, write a commit message, or needs git workflow help.
version: "1.2.0"
---

# Git Commit Helper

Full skill instructions go here. The AI reads this file when the skill is loaded.

## When to use me

- "help me commit these changes"
- "write a commit message"

## How I work

1. I examine your staged changes with `git diff --staged`
2. I suggest a conventional commit message
3. I confirm with you before running `git commit`
```

Frontmatter fields:

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Must match the skill `id` |
| `description` | Yes | One sentence — what the skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the keywords a user is likely to say. |
| `version` | No | Informational only |

---

## Publishing a New Skill Version

1. Update `version` in `skill.json` (e.g. `1.2.0` → `1.3.0`)
2. Update the matching `version` in `registry.json`
3. Update `updatedAt` in `registry.json`
4. Push to `main`

On the next opencode startup, the plugin detects the version bump and automatically installs the update. No user action required.

---

## Development

The package ships TypeScript source; opencode runs it directly, so there is no build step.

```bash
npm install        # dev dependencies (@opencode/plugin, typescript)
npm run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm run verify     # end-to-end suite against a stub GitLab server
```

`npm run verify` exercises install, update, remove, auto-update, config resolution, and the RPC
event schema against an in-process stand-in for the GitLab API. It redirects `HOME` to a temporary
directory first, so it never touches your real `~/.config/opencode`.

To test a local checkout, point a project's `.opencode/opencode.json` at it:

```json
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "file:/absolute/path/to/opencode-skills-marketplace" }]
}
```

The `file:` prefix and the `{ "package": ... }` object form are both required — a bare path is
silently ignored.

### Layout

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/index.ts` | Server plugin — owns the registry client, tools, command, and startup auto-update |
| `src/tui.ts` | CLI plugin — the marketplace dialogs; talks to the server half over RPC |
| `src/rpc.ts` | Shared wire contract between the two halves (zod schemas, no logic) |
| `src/service.ts` | Every marketplace operation, returning structured data |
| `src/gitlab.ts` | GitLab REST client |
| `src/sync.ts` | Install/remove/update and semver comparison |
| `src/state.ts` | `~/.config/opencode/marketplace-state.json` |
| `src/fmt.ts` | Markdown rendering for tool output |
